missing_token.description: CSRF token missing or not validated

probes.description: Submit form without CSRF token — check if action succeeds
Reuse old CSRF token in new session — check if accepted

method_override.description: CSRF bypass via HTTP method override

probes.description: Change POST to GET — many apps skip CSRF for GET

content_type_bypass.description: CSRF bypass via Content-Type change — some frameworks only validate CSRF for specific content types

probes.description: Change Content-Type to text/plain — simple form can cross-origin POST as text/plain without preflight
Change Content-Type to application/x-www-form-urlencoded — browser-native form type, no preflight needed

referer_bypass.description: CSRF bypass via Referer header manipulation — some apps rely on Referer instead of tokens

probes.description: Remove Referer header entirely — app may skip CSRF check if Referer absent
Set Referer: https://evil.com — app accepts requests from any origin (Referer not validated)

token_manipulation.description: CSRF token edge cases — empty, missing, or predictable token values

probes.description: Send empty CSRF token value — server may accept blank as valid
Delete CSRF token parameter entirely — server may only validate if present

samesite_bypass.description: SameSite cookie bypass -- exploit Lax+POST 2-minute window on Chromium, top-level navigation, and popup methods

probes.description: POST within 2 minutes of cookie set (Lax+POST window) -- Chromium sends SameSite=Lax cookies with cross-site POST for 2 min after creation
Top-level navigation via window.open -- SameSite=Lax allows GET on top-level navigations; chain with method conversion for POST actions

SameSite=Lax bypass via method override on a GET -- send the state-changing action as a top-level GET (Lax cookies attach) carrying _method=POST so the framework routes it to the POST handler. Bypasses Lax without needing the 2-minute window.

SameSite=Strict bypass via an on-site client-side-redirect gadget -- Strict cookies attach on any same-site request, so bounce through a same-site endpoint whose redirect parameter accepts a path-traversal value (e.g. /redirect?next=/../../admin/delete?id=1) to reach the target action from within the origin. The gadget performs the sensitive request itself, carrying the Strict cookie.

SameSite=Lax 2-minute window via window.open then delayed auto-submit -- window.open() establishes a fresh top-level navigation so Chromium treats subsequent cross-site POSTs as Lax-eligible for ~2 min; a setTimeout-delayed form auto-submit fires the state-changing POST inside that window.

CSRF token tied to a non-session cookie set independently via CRLF/response-splitting -- if the anti-CSRF token is validated against a cookie the attacker can plant (rather than the session), inject a Set-Cookie through a CRLF-reflecting parameter to fix both the cookie and the form token to the same known value, defeating double-submit.

method_conversion.description: CSRF via HTTP method conversion -- convert POST to GET to bypass CSRF protection, or exploit multipart boundary tricks

probes.description: Convert POST body to GET query string -- many frameworks route GET and POST to same handler but only check CSRF on POST
POST with _method=PUT override parameter -- framework method override may bypass CSRF middleware that only protects POST

json_csrf.description: CSRF for JSON API endpoints -- Content-Type manipulation to send JSON payloads via HTML forms without CORS preflight

probes.description: Send JSON body with Content-Type text/plain -- browsers allow cross-origin text/plain POST without preflight; server may still parse as JSON
JSON via form enctype with crafted name -- use form input name as JSON key to construct valid JSON body cross-origin
